question: Does the 2015 Marikina testis paper describe a separate male sample from the 2016 life-history paper, or the same 526-male component?

source.title: Histological and ultrastructural characteristics of the testis of the invasive suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Siluriformes: Loricariidae) from Marikina River, Philippines
source.citation: Jumawan, J. C., & Herrera, A. A. (2015). Histological and ultrastructural characteristics of the testis of the invasive suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Siluriformes: Loricariidae) from Marikina River, Philippines. Tissue and Cell, 47(1), 17-26. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tice.2014.10.005
source.accessMethod: Reviewed the PubMed bibliographic record and abstract, ScienceDirect search-indexed article information, a publicly rendered Scribd full-text repost for the methods and male sample count, and the 2016 ARPN publisher PDF. The Scribd uploader is not the publisher or an identified author; the repost is used only to verify cited study facts and does not establish authorized access or reuse. No file or figure was downloaded or retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The article is published by Elsevier and the public mirror labels rights as all rights reserved. No item-specific open reuse license was identified. This review summarizes citation, methods, aggregate sample and publication-lineage facts only; no article text, figure, map, table or measurements are redistributed.

studyDesign.sourceReportedTaxon: Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber 1991), as labeled by the article; identity is not independently resolved for this cohort.
studyDesign.gearAsReported: Cast net, 5 m long with 3.8 cm mesh.
studyDesign.histologySampleClarification: The paper reports 526 males collected and 360 testes samples fixed for histological work. The 360 tissue samples are subsamples/materials from the male study, not 360 additional fish.
studyDesign.stationAllocation: The article names five study sites but gives no site-by-site male counts or fish-to-station allocation. The station map is not digitized or treated as coordinate data.
studyDesign.voucherAndAccessionStatus: No specimen voucher, catalogue number, GenBank accession or individual record identifier was found in the reviewed article text.
studyDesign.studyPurpose: Describe testicular histology, ultrastructure, maturity stages and reproductive timing in source-labeled male Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus.
studyDesign.sourceIdentityCaveat: The 2016 paper notes Marikina barcode studies suggest unresolved P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus boundaries and possible introgressive hybridization. Preserve the species name as the 2015 paper source label only.

matchingAttributes: Both papers report 526 male fish from the same July 2010-June 2011 Marikina River collection.
Both describe the same five named collection sites: San Jose/Rodriguez Rizal, Banaba/San Mateo, Tumana, Malanday and River Park.
Both report the same 5 m cast net and 3.8 cm mesh specification.
The 2016 paper reports 607 females plus 526 males (1,133 total), and cites Jumawan and Herrera (2015) as the prior study of male gonad characteristics.
The 2015 paper says 526 males were collected; its 360 fixed testes samples are histology material and not a second fish cohort.
cohortCrosswalk.conclusion: High-confidence publication-level crosswalk: the 2015 testis study describes the male component of, or directly overlaps with, the 2016 526-male/607-female collection. Exact male count, period, sites and gear match, and the 2016 paper cites the earlier male-gonad study. Treat these as one male cohort for counting, not two independent surveys.
cohortCrosswalk.individualSpecimenLimit: Neither article provides a specimen-level identifier crosswalk proving that all 526 individual males are identical. Retain this as a high-confidence cohort-level match, not a specimen-voucher reconciliation.
cohortCrosswalk.countDecision: Count the 526 male field-sampled cohort once within the 2016 total of 1,133 fish. Do not add another 526 males for the 2015 article or count the 360 histology tissue samples as additional fish.

combined2014To2016Cohort.decision: The 2014 ovary paper and 2015 testis paper analyze female and male components that match the 2016 aggregate cohort. Use 1,133 as the single historical study sample total; do not sum across the three publications.

taxonomyAndOccurrenceDecision.relationship: The 2011 COI study reports a separate 36-fish Marikina sample and unresolved P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus/intermediate patterns. No voucher or accession connects that series to the 2015/2016 fish cohort.
taxonomyAndOccurrenceDecision.decision: Keep Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus only as an attributed publication label. Neither sex-specific aggregate nor five-site study design is a station-specific occurrence dataset; no coordinates, vouchers or site-level counts were recovered.

evidenceDecision.decision: Register the 2015 male testis paper as an analysis of the same historical male cohort reported in 2016, not a second independent sample. Count 526 males once; combine with the separately crosswalked 607 females for the single 1,133-fish historical cohort.

nonClaims: The 2015 and 2016 papers are not two independent groups of 526 males; available evidence strongly indicates a shared male cohort, while individual identity is not proven.
The 360 fixed testes samples described for histology are not 360 additional fish and must not be counted as additional individual fish.
The 2014, 2015 and 2016 articles are related analyses of sex-specific components of one reported 2010-2011 collection, not three independent surveys.
Neither article provides station-specific sample counts, so the 526 males and 607 females cannot be allocated among five sites or assigned to NCR/Rizal separately.
Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus remains a source-reported name, not a specimen-verified identification for the aggregate samples.
No current occurrence, abundance, catchability, legal status, food/water safety, diet guidance, map geometry or public app row follows from this cohort crosswalk.
nextActions: Retain the 2014/2015/2016 sample as one 1,133-fish historical Marikina cohort in any future research tally.
Do not import site-map positions or allocate male/female counts to individual stations; require a source-provided sample-to-station dataset.
Resolve the Pterygoplichthys label only with diagnostic specimen or sequence evidence tied to the 2010-2011 cohort.
